# Drill candidate axis: rules and the schema objects that hold them

Phase 1's shadow ledger (`shadow.db`) records every run the drill selector looked at
(`drill_candidate`), the time zone its day keys are drawn in (`drill_day_zone`), and the
attempts planned for a selected run (`drill_attempt`). Each rule below names the CHECK
constraint, trigger or index that holds it in the shipped migrations, so a constraint
violation reaches the operator under the same name this table uses.

A test builds the schema from the shipped migrations and checks the names in both
directions (every name here exists, and every named object on these tables is listed
here), then writes rows each rule allows and forbids and requires SQLite to refuse the
forbidden ones with an error attributed to the named object.

Rules without a name are held by a structural constraint SQLite does not name (a
foreign key, a UNIQUE column), by the absence of a constraint, or by an order, which no
CHECK can express.

## Rules

| # | Table | Rule | Held by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `drill_day_zone` | The interpretation of a day key is a separate record and has NO foreign key to `drill_day`. It must outlive the days it explains; with a foreign key, retention would delete the only record of which time zone the surviving keys were drawn in. | — *absence of a constraint*: The absence of a foreign key. `shadow.Retain` never deletes from this table. |
| 2 | `drill_day_zone` | `since_day` has the same shape as a day key (`YYYY-MM-DD`); a timestamp cannot be written. | `drill_day_zone_since_day_shape` |
| 3 | `drill_day_zone` | `timezone` is an IANA zone name, not an offset, and cannot be empty. | `drill_day_zone_timezone_nonempty` |
| 4 | `drill_day_zone` | A zone row is append-only: rewriting it would retroactively change which calendar day every key since `since_day` names. | `drill_day_zone_append_only` |
| 5 | `drill_candidate` | A candidate falls on a day the ledger has recorded. | — *structural constraint*: Foreign key `drill_candidate.drill_day` → `drill_day(day)`. |
| 6 | `drill_candidate` | The identity of the selector that made the decision is recorded. The inputs are not enough; which selector looked at them is needed too. | `drill_candidate_selector_rev_nonempty` |
| 7 | `drill_candidate` | `source` has two values: `github_history` (the drill's main path) and `synthetic` (a run the ref prober proposes that has no counterpart on GitHub). | `drill_candidate_source_enum` |
| 8 | `drill_candidate` | `commit_sha` is exactly 40 characters. | `drill_candidate_commit_sha_len` |
| 9 | `drill_candidate` | `github_run_attempt ≥ 1`. | `drill_candidate_run_attempt_positive` |
| 10 | `drill_candidate` | `github_conclusion` is one of GitHub's nine conclusion values (including `startup_failure`), and never `in_progress`, which is a value of `status`. The set is deliberately not narrowed to the values observed so far: not having been observed is not evidence of absence. | `drill_candidate_github_conclusion_enum` |
| 11 | `drill_candidate` | A history-path row carries `github_run_id`, `github_created_at` and `github_run_attempt`; a synthetic row carries none of them. The bond is two-way. | `drill_candidate_history_has_run_id`, `drill_candidate_history_has_created_at`, `drill_candidate_history_has_run_attempt` |
| 12 | `drill_candidate` | The deferral queue is in GitHub's own order: `github_created_at` ascending, oldest first. The sort key reads nothing from our side, so no ranking of ours can put the hard runs off indefinitely. | — *order (code path)*: The column itself; the deferral-queue audit query reads the order. No CHECK can hold an ORDER BY. |
| 13 | `drill_candidate` | `disposition` has seven values and none of them refers to our ability to run something. An eighth value is a schema change. | `drill_candidate_disposition_enum` |
| 14 | `drill_candidate` | The prefilter cannot eliminate a history-path run. GitHub created that run; our filter disagreeing is a finding, not a reason to drop it. | `drill_candidate_history_dispositions` |
| 15 | `drill_candidate` | `not_created` and `undecidable` exist only on the synthetic path. (Today rule 14's constraint refuses every violating row first; this one is defence in depth against a widened `source`.) | `drill_candidate_prefilter_dispositions_are_synthetic` |
| 16 | `drill_candidate` | A synthetic candidate never enters the score: `selected` and `deferred` are both forbidden for it. Otherwise a verdict GitHub never gave would flow straight into the gate's numerator. | `drill_candidate_synthetic_never_enters_the_score` |
| 17 | `drill_candidate` | `selected` requires a conclusion; `not_concluded` cannot carry one. | `drill_candidate_selected_needs_conclusion`, `drill_candidate_not_concluded_has_no_conclusion` |
| 18 | `drill_candidate` | Not being selected always carries a sentence; a reasonless exclusion cannot be written. `deferred` is included on purpose: a cap that does not say which cap is a hiding place. | `drill_candidate_exclusion_has_a_reason` |
| 19 | `drill_candidate` | The detail of `out_of_scope` is one of three closed words: `shadow_never`, `not_configured`, `github_internal_workflow`. | `drill_candidate_out_of_scope_detail_enum` |
| 20 | `drill_candidate` | A `dynamic/` workflow path ⟺ `out_of_scope` with `github_internal_workflow`, in both directions. It follows that `out_of_scope` beats `not_concluded` on such a path. The prefix test is case-sensitive. | `drill_candidate_github_internal_is_dynamic_path` |
| 21 | `drill_candidate` | A GitHub run is selected at most once, ever. The gate counts distinct runs and its denominator query counts rows. (Partial UNIQUE index.) | `idx_drill_candidate_selected_once` |
| 22 | `drill_candidate` | A candidate row is append-only: looking at a run again is a NEW row (`already_selected`); rewriting the old one would erase what the selector once said. | `drill_candidate_append_only` |
| 23 | `drill_candidate` | The deferral-queue audit query does not scan: the partial index covers `deferred` AND `not_concluded` together. | `idx_drill_candidate_open` |
| 24 | `drill_candidate` | The per-day disposition breakdown reads from an index. | `idx_drill_candidate_day` |
| 25 | `drill_attempt` | An attempt row is written BEFORE the process is invoked, with `invocation_id` NULL. A run we selected and failed to run must not look the same in the ledger as a run we never selected. | — *order (code path)*: `invocation_id` being nullable; the order is held by `RunDay` and read by the planned-but-uninvoked audit query. No CHECK can hold an order. |
| 26 | `drill_attempt` | `supply_mode` has two values (`online`, `offline`) and the programme is paired: a selected candidate is attempted in both. | `drill_attempt_supply_mode_enum` |
| 27 | `drill_attempt` | An attempt is planned only for a `selected` candidate. Otherwise the executor could run a candidate whose disposition says `out_of_scope`, and each half of the ledger would look sound on its own. | `drill_attempt_only_for_selected` |
| 28 | `drill_attempt` | After planning only `invocation_id` may be written; `candidate_id`, `supply_mode` and `planned_at` are write-once. | `drill_attempt_write_once` |
| 29 | `drill_attempt` | `invocation_id` is written once. Re-pointing it at a second invocation would replace a run that went badly with a better one after the fact. | `drill_attempt_invocation_write_once` |
| 30 | `drill_attempt` | An invocation belongs to at most one attempt. | — *structural constraint*: `drill_attempt.invocation_id` is UNIQUE. |

## Ledger tables

Every table the `shadow.db` migrations build. A test compares this list with the schema
in both directions, so a new table cannot ship unlisted.

| Table | Axis | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | bookkeeping | Applied migrations and their checksums. |
| `drill_day` | day | One row for every day of the drill window, including why a day has no runs. |
| `exec_invocation` | run | One executor invocation, written in two phases: opened before the process, closed after it. |
| `exec_image` | run | The image used for each `runs-on` label of an invocation, with the configured source digest. |
| `exec_local_repository` | run | The HEAD of each local action mirror, read before the run, so a stale mirror is auditable. |
| `exec_job_result` | run | Per-job results of an invocation. |
| `exec_step_observation` | run | Step-level records observed during an invocation. |
| `exec_residue` | run | Containers and volumes an invocation left behind (counted, not cleaned). |
| `exec_note` | run | Free-text notes the executor produced, stored verbatim. |
| `drill_day_zone` | candidate | The time zone day keys are drawn in, from a given day on. |
| `drill_candidate` | candidate | Every run the selector looked at, with its disposition and reason. |
| `drill_attempt` | candidate | The planned attempts for a selected candidate, one per supply mode. |
